background: Son of longtime NBA coach Bernie Bickerstaff, J.B. became an NBA assistant at 25 (Charlotte, 2004) and served interim head-coaching stints with Houston (2015-16, 37-34, playoffs) and Memphis (2017-19) before taking over Cleveland in February 2020. He led the Cavaliers' rebuild into a 51-win team and the league's No. 1 defense (2022-23) and a second-round appearance (2024), but was fired in May 2024 amid criticism of his half-court offense and playoff adjustments. Detroit hired him in July 2024 after a 14-68 season; he immediately delivered a 30-win improvement (44-38, first playoff appearance since 2019 and first playoff win since 2008), finished runner-up for Coach of the Year, then went 60-22 in 2025-26 as the East's No. 1 seed, won a first-round series over Orlando and lost a home Game 7 to Cleveland in the second round. Extended in May 2026. Reputation: physical, aggressive, foul-heavy defense; culture and accountability; a Cade Cunningham-centric, paint- and glass-oriented offense with low three-point volume.

evidence: Pistons ran a conventional 9-10 man rotation in 2024-25 and 2025-26 with veteran role players (Beasley, Hardaway, Harris, Robinson, LeVert) absorbing bench minutes; Cavaliers rotations under him were 9 deep with a fixed top eight (background knowledge; not re-verified).

Cade Cunningham averaged roughly 35 mpg in 2024-25 and Donovan Mitchell/Darius Garland played 35-36 mpg in Cleveland under Bickerstaff; he leans on his stars heavily when healthy (background knowledge; not re-verified).

Prefers a fixed starting five and set roles (Cleveland's double-big lineup for three seasons; Detroit's Cunningham-Thompson-Duren core); rotation changes are usually injury-driven rather than matchup churn (background knowledge).

Started Ausar Thompson and Jalen Duren (both 22 or younger) and gave 19-20-year-old Ron Holland a rotation role in Detroit, and trusted rookie Evan Mobley in Cleveland; but favored veterans Beasley/Hardaway over Ivey/Holland in 2024-25 closing lineups (background knowledge).
Cleveland frequently rested Mitchell/Garland for injury management; in Detroit, Cunningham played most games and the Pistons' 60-win pursuit of the top seed left little room for rest (inferred).

Closing group has been stable: Cunningham plus Thompson, Duren and two shooters; Cleveland closed with the Mitchell-Garland-Mobley-Allen core regardless of matchup, a point of playoff criticism (background knowledge).

Cavaliers under Bickerstaff ranked in the bottom third in pace (methodical, half-court); Pistons have been closer to league average, driven by Thompson/Cunningham transition off turnovers (background knowledge; 2025-26 rank not retrieved).

Pistons ranked in the bottom tier of three-point attempt rate in 2024-25 and 2025-26 with two traditional bigs (Duren, Stewart) often sharing the floor; Cleveland's Allen-Mobley teams were also below average in 3PA rate (background knowledge).

Offense is Cunningham-centric (roughly 9 assists per game on very high usage) with heavy on-ball pick-and-roll; Cleveland's offense was Mitchell/Garland isolation-heavy and criticized for stagnation in the 2023 playoffs (background knowledge).
Detroit converts steals from its physical defense into transition (Thompson), but the base system is half-court; Cleveland teams were slow (inferred).

Pistons have been among the league's best offensive-rebounding teams with Duren, Stewart and Thompson crashing, and Cleveland's Allen/Mobley double-big also ranked highly on the offensive glass (background knowledge; exact ranks not retrieved).
Two-big lineups, Duren rim-running, Cunningham downhill drives and second-chance points make Detroit one of the most paint-centric offenses; low 3PA volume reinforces this (background knowledge).

Persistent criticism in Cleveland of predictable, iso-heavy late-game and after-timeout offense, especially in the 2023 series vs New York; Detroit's offense ranked well below its defense in 2024-25 (background knowledge).

Detroit's defense under Bickerstaff is built on physicality, point-of-attack pressure from Thompson/Holland and heavy contact at the rim; Cleveland was a conservative drop/wall-off team with elite rim protection (background knowledge).
Drop coverage with Duren (DET) and Allen/Mobley (CLE) prioritizes the paint and concedes some threes; the Cavs' No. 1 defense in 2022-23 was a rim-protection scheme (background knowledge).
Pistons were among the league leaders in personal fouls and opponent free-throw attempts in 2024-25, an accepted cost of their physical identity (background knowledge; not re-verified).
Occasional zone possessions in both Cleveland and Detroit, but primarily a man-to-man drop team (inferred).

Criticized for rigidity in playoff series (Cleveland 2023 vs NYK, 2024 vs BOS; Detroit's Game 7 blowout loss to Cleveland in 2026); tends to trust base scheme and personnel rather than change coverages (background knowledge plus 2026 Game 7 reporting).
